intent.raw_query: Vietnam on $800, backpacking 10 days, street food and culture, April 2026

experiences.name: Hanoi Old Quarter Street Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the labyrinthine streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter on foot, sampling iconic Vietnamese dishes including Bun Cha, Banh Mi, Pho, and Egg Coffee from legendary local vendors and hole-in-the-wall eateries. Join a budget walking tour or self-guide using a street food map.

experiences.name: Hoi An Ancient Town Lantern Festival & Night Market
experiences.description: Wander through the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town of Hoi An, admiring centuries-old merchant houses, temples, and colorful silk lanterns. Visit the bustling night market, try Cao Lau and White Rose dumplings from street stalls, and release a lantern on the Thu Bon River for good luck.

experiences.name: Halong Bay Budget Kayaking & Cave Exploration
experiences.description: Join an affordable group day tour or budget overnight cruise through the stunning limestone karsts of Halong Bay. Kayak through hidden lagoons, explore Sung Sot (Surprise) Cave, and swim in emerald waters. Budget operators offer backpacker-friendly prices without sacrificing the iconic scenery.

experiences.name: Hue Imperial Citadel & Royal Tomb Bicycle Tour
experiences.description: Rent a bicycle and explore the historic Imperial Citadel, the Forbidden Purple City, and the ornate royal tombs of the Nguyen Dynasty scattered along the Perfume River. Stop at local com hen (clam rice) stalls and banh khoai (crispy pancake) vendors for authentic Hue cuisine along the way.

experiences.name: Ho Chi Minh City Ben Thanh Market & War Remnants Museum
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the energy of Saigon by visiting the historic Ben Thanh Market for fresh tropical fruits, Vietnamese coffee, and local snacks. Then visit the powerful War Remnants Museum to gain deep cultural and historical insight into Vietnam's modern history. End the day with a bowl of Hu Tieu noodle soup from a sidewalk vendor.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Vietnam
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: N/A - Flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A - Flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear immigration and customs, exchange a small amount of cash (USD to VND) at the airport money changer. Take a pre-booked airport taxi or grab app ride to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled. If hungry, ask hotel staff about any nearby 24-hour street food stalls or convenience stores (Circle K or Vinmart are common and budget-friendly).

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane
meals.dinner: Late-night snack from a nearby convenience store or 24-hour pho stall near the hotel (~30,000-50,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — just arrive safely and rest. Download the Grab app before landing for cheap and reliable transport. Have small USD bills ready for tips or emergencies.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After waking, head to a local Vietnamese breakfast spot near the hotel. Enjoy a bowl of Bún bò Huế or Bánh mì from a street vendor. Walk around the immediate neighborhood to get your bearings, locate a local SIM card shop (Viettel or Vietnamobile offer budget SIMs for ~100,000 VND with data).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the beachfront area on foot. Visit the local market nearest to the resort to browse fresh produce, snacks, and souvenirs. Pick up cheap tropical fruits like dragon fruit, rambutan, or mangosteen from street vendors. Stroll along the beach promenade and observe local life.
day_by_day.evening: Find a local seafood street food area near the beachfront. Try grilled corn, skewered meats, or fresh seafood cooked to order at open-air stalls. Watch the sunset from the beach. Return to the hotel early to plan the upcoming days.

meals.breakfast: Street-side Bánh mì or Xôi (sticky rice) from a local vendor (~20,000-40,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Local com binh dan (rice plate) restaurant with meat, vegetables and soup (~40,000-60,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Beachfront street food stalls — grilled seafood, corn, and skewers (~80,000-120,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Buy a local SIM card today — it will save money on maps, Grab rides, and communication throughout the trip. Budget approximately 200,000-300,000 VND for the full day including food and transport.

day_by_day.date: Day 3 - April 17 (Culture & Street Food Deep Dive)
day_by_day.morning: Wake up early (6:00-7:00 AM) to experience the morning street food scene at its peak. Visit a local wet market to watch vendors and try fresh Phở or Hủ tiếu from a market stall. After breakfast, visit the nearest pagoda or Buddhist temple in the area — entrance is usually free and the atmosphere is serene in the morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle or motorbike from the hotel or a local shop (~80,000-150,000 VND/day) and explore the surrounding villages and countryside. Visit a local craft village or fishing village if accessible. Stop at a roadside café for a Vietnamese iced coffee (cà phê sữa đá) — a must-try at ~20,000-30,000 VND.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the main town area and explore the night market or evening street food scene. Try Bánh xèo (sizzling crepes), Gỏi cuốn (fresh spring rolls), and Chè (Vietnamese sweet dessert soup) from different stalls.

meals.breakfast: Market Phở or Hủ tiếu (~30,000-50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Roadside Cơm tấm (broken rice with pork) (~40,000-70,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Night market street food spread — try 3-4 different dishes (~80,000-120,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Haggle politely at markets — it's expected. Always smile and be respectful. Motorbike rental requires a valid license; check local rules. Carry small denomination VND notes for street food vendors.

day_by_day.date: Day 4 - April 18 (Day Trip to Nearby Cultural Site)
day_by_day.morning: Pack a small daypack and take an early Grab or local bus to the nearest historically or culturally significant town or site (e.g., a UNESCO heritage site, old town, or ancient citadel depending on the resort's location). Arrive by 9:00 AM to beat the heat and crowds. Explore temples, old architecture, and local history on foot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the cultural site. Have lunch at a local eatery in the old town area. Browse local craft shops and pick up inexpensive handmade souvenirs. Wander through alleyways and photograph traditional architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area by early evening. Wind down with a walk along the beach. Find a local Lẩu (hot pot) restaurant and enjoy a budget communal hot pot dinner — great for solo backpackers to meet other travelers.

meals.breakfast: Grab something light from a street vendor before departing (~20,000-30,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Local restaurant in the cultural site area — Cao lầu or Mì Quảng if available (~50,000-80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Budget hot pot restaurant near the hotel (~100,000-150,000 VND per person)

day_by_day.notes: Research the nearest UNESCO or heritage site to your resort location in advance. Local buses are the cheapest transport option (~20,000-50,000 VND each way). Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring sunscreen and water.

day_by_day.morning: Start the morning with a sunrise beach walk or swim. Many Vietnamese locals do morning exercises on the beach — join in for a cultural experience. Grab a cheap breakfast from a beachside vendor. If the resort area has kayak or paddleboard rentals, opt for the most budget-friendly option (kayak rentals often start at ~100,000-150,000 VND/hour).
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore nearby islands or snorkeling spots via a local budget boat tour (look for group tours at ~200,000-300,000 VND per person rather than private charters). Alternatively, explore hidden beaches accessible by motorbike. Bring your own snacks and water to save money.
day_by_day.evening: Relax on the beach and watch the sunset. Head to a local seafood restaurant away from tourist traps — look for places where locals eat. Order fresh fish, clams, or shrimp cooked simply with salt, pepper, and lime.

meals.breakfast: Beachside Bánh mì or fruit smoothie (~30,000-50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks from the market or eat on the boat tour (~50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Local seafood restaurant — grilled fish + rice + vegetables (~100,000-150,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Avoid overpriced tourist beach clubs. Ask your hotel staff where locals go for the best budget seafood. Apply reef-safe sunscreen for snorkeling to protect marine ecosystems. Stay hydrated in the heat.

day_by_day.date: Day 6 - April 20 (Street Food Cooking & Local Market Tour)
day_by_day.morning: Join a budget street food walking tour or a local cooking class (many guesthouses offer these for ~200,000-350,000 VND). Visit a local morning market with the guide to pick up fresh ingredients. Learn about Vietnamese herbs, spices, and cooking techniques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cook and eat your own Vietnamese meal if participating in a class. Alternatively, spend the afternoon visiting a local fishing harbor to watch boats come in with the day's catch. Chat with fishermen and observe the lively atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local Bia hơi (fresh draft beer) street corner — a quintessential Vietnamese backpacker experience. Sit on tiny plastic stools, drink cheap draft beer (~5,000-10,000 VND per glass), and snack on peanuts and grilled meats with fellow travelers and locals.

meals.breakfast: Included in cooking class or market breakfast (~30,000-50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Dishes made in the cooking class or local com binh dan (~50,000-80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Bia hơi corner with snacks and grilled skewers (~60,000-100,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Bia hơi culture is uniquely Vietnamese and extremely budget-friendly. Always eat and drink where locals are sitting — it's a reliable sign of good quality and fair prices. Cooking classes are excellent value and a memorable experience.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a motorbike and head inland to explore rice paddies, farming villages, and natural landscapes away from the coast. Stop at small villages to observe traditional Vietnamese rural life. Visit a local family-run coffee plantation or rice farm if accessible.
day_by_day.afternoon: Find a scenic viewpoint or hill for panoramic views of the surrounding landscape. Pack a picnic lunch from the morning market to save money. Explore any nearby waterfalls, caves, or nature reserves (entrance fees are usually minimal, ~20,000-50,000 VND).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel and freshen up. Treat yourself to a budget Vietnamese massage (~150,000-200,000 VND for 60 minutes) — widely available and excellent value. Have a simple, relaxed dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Local sticky rice or Bánh cuốn (steamed rice rolls) from a street stall (~25,000-40,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Picnic from the market — fruits, bread, and snacks (~50,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Simple noodle soup or rice dish near the hotel (~40,000-60,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Always wear a helmet when riding a motorbike — it's the law and essential for safety. Bring a paper map as a backup in case of poor mobile signal in rural areas. Inform the hotel of your general route before heading out.

day_by_day.morning: Visit a local museum, cultural center, or heritage house in the nearest town. Many are free or charge a minimal entrance fee (~20,000-40,000 VND). Learn about the history of the region, local ethnic minority groups, and traditional Vietnamese customs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a handicraft village or artisan workshop — lacquerware, silk weaving, pottery, or lantern making depending on the region. Watch artisans at work and buy small, affordable handmade items directly from the makers to support local livelihoods.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost cultural performance if available (water puppetry shows, traditional music, or folk dance performances are common in tourist areas for ~60,000-100,000 VND). Follow up with dinner at a local vegetarian restaurant — Buddhist vegetarian food (cơm chay) is delicious and very cheap in Vietnam.

meals.breakfast: Dim sum-style Vietnamese breakfast — Bánh bao (steamed buns) and soy milk (~30,000-50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Street food near the handicraft village (~50,000-80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Buddhist vegetarian restaurant (cơm chay) — full meal for (~40,000-70,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Vegetarian Buddhist restaurants are incredibly cheap and offer generous portions. Look for restaurants with a yellow flag or 'Cơm Chay' sign. Cultural performances are usually worth the small cost for an authentic experience.

day_by_day.morning: Use the morning for any activities or places you missed earlier in the trip. Revisit a favorite spot, take final photos, or simply enjoy a slow breakfast at a local café. Write postcards or journal entries about the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to a local market for souvenir shopping. Look for budget-friendly gifts: dried fruits, Vietnamese coffee, tea, lacquerware, conical hats (nón lá), silk scarves, or hand-painted postcards. Bargain respectfully. Pack your bags and reorganize your backpack for the journey home.
day_by_day.evening: Have a farewell street food feast — revisit your favorite dishes from the trip. Try anything you haven't eaten yet. Enjoy a final sunset on the beach and reflect on the journey. Have an early night to prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Slow café breakfast — Vietnamese egg coffee (cà phê trứng) if available + pastry (~40,000-60,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Revisit your favorite street food spot from the trip (~50,000-80,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Farewell street food spread — order all your favorites (~100,000-150,000 VND)

day_by_day.notes: Budget approximately 200,000-400,000 VND for souvenirs. Vietnamese coffee (whole bean or ground) makes an excellent, lightweight, and affordable gift. Avoid buying items made from wildlife or protected species.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early, enjoy a final Vietnamese breakfast near the hotel. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Store luggage at the hotel if your flight is later in the day. Take one last walk along the beach or through the local neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your flight time, spend remaining hours at a local café working or relaxing. Use up any remaining VND on snacks, drinks, or last-minute purchases (VND is difficult to exchange outside Vietnam). Head to the airport with plenty of time — allow 2-3 hours before departure for check-in and security.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Vietnam. Reflect on an incredible budget backpacking adventure filled with street food, culture, and unforgettable experiences.

meals.breakfast: Final Vietnamese breakfast — Phở or Bánh mì (~30,000-50,000 VND)
meals.lunch: Airport food or nearby café before departure (~60,000-100,000 VND)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Exchange or spend all remaining VND before leaving — it cannot be easily converted abroad. Keep a small emergency fund in USD until you board. Take a Grab to the airport for the most reliable and budget-friendly option. Safe travels!

trip_options.title: Classic Vietnam Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — flight in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at destination airport at 22:30 on Flight UA. Clear immigration and customs, collect baggage, and arrange airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get settled into your beachfront room.

meals.breakfast: On flight or airport snack
meals.lunch: On flight or airport food court
meals.dinner: Late-night street food near the resort or hotel in-house dining — try a simple bowl of Pho or Banh Mi from a nearby 24-hour stall if available

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Confirm your check-in with the resort in advance for a smooth late-night arrival. Exchange some currency at the airport for immediate expenses. Rest well — big days ahead!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely wake-up, take a relaxed stroll along the beachfront near Aegean Bliss Resort. Breathe in the sea air and get oriented with your surroundings. Visit a nearby local market to pick up snacks and get a feel for the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the nearest town or village on foot or by rented bicycle. Visit a local pagoda or temple for a taste of Vietnamese spiritual culture. Browse small shops and observe everyday Vietnamese life in the area.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a lively street food alley or night market near the resort. Sample local specialties and soak in the vibrant atmosphere of Vietnamese evening culture.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast or a local cafe — try Banh Mi with iced Vietnamese coffee (ca phe sua da)
meals.lunch: Local com binh dan (everyday rice plate) restaurant — rice with grilled pork, pickled vegetables, and soup for under $3
meals.dinner: Night market street food — try Bun Bo Hue (spicy beef noodle soup), fresh spring rolls, and grilled skewers

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a local SIM card today for affordable data throughout the trip. Rent a bicycle from the resort or a nearby shop for easy local exploration — typically $3–5/day.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for a sunrise walk or jog along the beach. After breakfast, visit a nearby heritage site, fishing village, or cultural landmark. Engage with locals and learn about the region's history and traditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a half-day cooking class or street food tour in the local area. Learn to make iconic Vietnamese dishes like fresh spring rolls, Pho broth, or Banh Xeo (sizzling crepes). This is an immersive cultural and culinary experience.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at a beachside bar or cafe with a cold Bia Hoi (fresh draft beer, very affordable) and watch the sunset. Enjoy a casual dinner at a mid-range local seafood restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Congee (chao) with ginger and scallions at a local breakfast stall
meals.lunch: Included in cooking class, or grab Banh Cuon (steamed rice rolls) from a street vendor
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood at a local open-air restaurant — grilled prawns, clams with lemongrass, and steamed fish with rice ($8–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Cooking classes typically cost $20–35 per person and are worth every cent for the cultural immersion. Book in advance if possible through the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to a nearby natural attraction — a national park, waterfall, cave system, or scenic viewpoint depending on your resort's region. Hire a local guide or join a small group tour for context and safety.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the day trip with a picnic lunch in nature, a short hike, or a boat ride through scenic waterways. Capture photos and enjoy Vietnam's stunning natural landscapes.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by late afternoon. Freshen up and head out for a relaxed evening exploring local alleyways, trying street snacks, and people-watching at a busy corner cafe.

meals.breakfast: Xoi (sticky rice with toppings) from a morning street cart — filling and cheap at ~$1
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a local deli or roadside stall during the day trip — Banh Mi or rice boxes
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant dinner — try Ca Kho To (caramelized fish in clay pot) with steamed rice and vegetables

day_by_day.notes: Day trips typically cost $15–40 per person depending on the destination. Wear sunscreen, carry water, and wear comfortable shoes for outdoor exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day — take a scenic bus, train, or budget flight to Hoi An (or your next destination). Enjoy the journey and the changing Vietnamese landscapes along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Hoi An. Check into a mid-range guesthouse or hostel in the Old Town area. Drop your bags and take a slow walk through the UNESCO-listed Ancient Town, admiring the lantern-lit streets and colonial architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Hoi An's famous lantern-lit Old Town at dusk — the most magical time to visit. Cross the iconic Japanese Covered Bridge, browse silk shops, and soak in the romantic atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast at the resort before departure — Pho or toast with eggs
meals.lunch: On the road — convenience store snacks, or stop at a roadside com tam (broken rice) stall
meals.dinner: Hoi An specialty dinner — Cao Lau (local thick noodles with pork and herbs) and White Rose dumplings at a traditional restaurant in the Old Town ($5–10)

day_by_day.notes: Hoi An's Old Town entrance tickets cost around $5 for access to heritage sites. The town is best explored on foot. Evening is the best time to see the lanterns reflected on the Thu Bon River.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Hoi An's Central Market early in the morning to witness the bustling trade of fresh produce, spices, and street food. Then explore the Assembly Halls (Fujian, Cantonese) and traditional merchant houses for deep cultural insight.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle and ride to the nearby villages — visit Tra Que Vegetable Village where farmers grow herbs used in local cuisine, or cycle to An Bang Beach for a relaxing afternoon by the sea.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Old Town for the famous Hoi An Night Market. Browse handmade lanterns, clothing, and souvenirs. Enjoy street food along the riverside promenade.

meals.breakfast: Banh Mi Phuong — Hoi An's most famous Banh Mi shop, beloved by Anthony Bourdain (~$1.50)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood at An Bang Beach shack — grilled fish, squid, and cold beer with ocean views ($6–10)
meals.dinner: Night market street food feast — Mi Quang noodles, Banh Vac dumplings, and fresh sugarcane juice

day_by_day.notes: Hoi An is extremely walkable and bicycle-friendly. Bicycle rentals cost $1–2/day. The town can get crowded midday — early mornings and evenings offer the most authentic atmosphere.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to My Son Sanctuary — an ancient Cham Hindu temple complex set in a jungle valley, dating back to the 4th century. Hire a local guide to understand the rich history of the Cham civilization.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Hoi An and spend the afternoon exploring the less-touristed back streets of the Old Town. Visit a local tailor if interested in having custom clothing made (Hoi An is famous for this — budget $30–80 for a custom piece).
day_by_day.evening: Take a lantern boat ride on the Thu Bon River at sunset. Release a floating lantern for good luck — a beautiful and meaningful Vietnamese tradition.

meals.breakfast: Xoi Ga (sticky rice with chicken) from a local morning stall near your guesthouse
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local family restaurant near My Son — simple Vietnamese home cooking with rice and multiple dishes
meals.dinner: Upscale-casual Vietnamese restaurant in Hoi An — try a set menu with spring rolls, pho, and grilled meats ($12–18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: My Son tours typically cost $10–20 including transport. Book through your guesthouse or a local agency. The lantern boat ride costs around $2–5 per person — a must-do Hoi An experience.

day_by_day.morning: Travel to Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City (depending on trip direction) via budget flight or overnight train. If flying, arrive by midday. Check into your accommodation and rest briefly.
day_by_day.afternoon: If in Hanoi: Explore Hoan Kiem Lake, Ngoc Son Temple, and the surrounding streets of the Old Quarter. If in Ho Chi Minh City: Visit Ben Thanh Market and the surrounding District 1 streets for an urban street food crawl.
day_by_day.evening: Join the evening street life — in Hanoi, visit the famous Bia Hoi Corner (corner of Ta Hien and Luong Ngoc Quyen) for $0.30 draft beers and snacks. In HCMC, explore Bui Vien Walking Street for a buzzing backpacker atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: On the move — airport or train station food
meals.lunch: Bun Cha (Hanoi) — grilled pork with vermicelli noodles and dipping broth, or Hu Tieu (HCMC) — Southern-style noodle soup ($2–4)
meals.dinner: Street food dinner at the Old Quarter or District 1 — try local specialties like Pho, Goi Cuon, and Che desserts

day_by_day.notes: Budget flights between Hoi An/Da Nang and Hanoi or HCMC cost $20–60 if booked in advance. VietJet Air and Bamboo Airways are reliable budget carriers. Keep luggage minimal for easy movement.

day_by_day.morning: In Hanoi: Visit the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex, One Pillar Pagoda, and the Temple of Literature — Vietnam's first university. In HCMC: Visit the War Remnants Museum and Reunification Palace for a powerful historical perspective.
day_by_day.afternoon: In Hanoi: Explore the Vietnam Museum of Ethnology or wander through the vibrant 36 Streets of the Old Quarter, each historically dedicated to a specific trade. In HCMC: Explore Cholon (Chinatown), the Binh Tay Market, and Thien Hau Temple.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a farewell-style dinner at a well-regarded mid-range Vietnamese restaurant. Enjoy a cultural performance if available — water puppetry in Hanoi is a world-class traditional art form.

meals.breakfast: Pho Bo (beef pho) at a classic local pho shop — the quintessential Vietnamese breakfast ($2–3)
meals.lunch: Bun Dau Mam Tom (Hanoi) — fried tofu and vermicelli with shrimp paste dip, or Banh Xeo (HCMC) — sizzling crepes with shrimp and bean sprouts
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant dinner — a spread of Vietnamese sharing dishes including spring rolls, braised pork belly, and stir-fried morning glory ($15–25 for two)

day_by_day.notes: Water puppet shows in Hanoi run multiple times daily and cost around $5–8. Book tickets in advance at the Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre. Dress modestly when visiting temples and government sites.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning exploration — revisit a favorite neighborhood or spot you didn't get enough of. Pick up last-minute souvenirs: Vietnamese coffee, silk scarves, lacquerware, or handmade crafts from local artisan shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Enjoy a final Vietnamese lunch at a beloved local spot. Head back to your accommodation, pack up, and prepare for departure. Allow ample time for airport transfer — Vietnam's city traffic can be unpredictable.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Vietnam with incredible memories, a full stomach, and a deep appreciation for this vibrant country's food, culture, and people.

meals.breakfast: One last Banh Mi and Vietnamese iced coffee from a street vendor — the perfect send-off
meals.lunch: Final splurge lunch at a well-loved local restaurant — order your favorite dish from the trip one last time
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. Keep some Vietnamese Dong for last-minute purchases, or spend it at the airport. Most airports have good duty-free shops with local products.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Vietnam Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities scheduled — late night arrival at 22:30
day_by_day.evening: Arrive via Flight UA at 22:30. Private airport transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in, unwind with a welcome drink at the resort's beachfront lounge, and settle into your luxury suite.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable
meals.lunch: Not applicable
meals.dinner: Light late-night welcome platter and cocktails arranged by the resort upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Ensure private transfer is pre-booked. Request early check-in amenities such as chilled towels, fruit basket, and sparkling wine in the room. Keep Day 1 light to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort's signature restaurant overlooking the beachfront. Afterwards, take a private guided orientation walk along the nearby coastal village to get acquainted with the local surroundings and culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Embark on a curated cultural excursion to a nearby historic town or fishing village. Explore traditional craft workshops, visit a local pagoda, and interact with artisans. A premium private guide provides historical context throughout.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a sunset cocktail hour at the beach bar. Enjoy a premium multi-course Vietnamese dinner at the resort's fine-dining restaurant featuring locally sourced ingredients.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at the resort's beachfront restaurant — Vietnamese pho, fresh tropical fruits, eggs Benedict, and freshly brewed Vietnamese ca phe (coffee)
meals.lunch: Private picnic-style lunch curated by the resort chef, enjoyed at a scenic coastal or village viewpoint
meals.dinner: Fine-dining Vietnamese tasting menu at the resort — featuring dishes like chả giò (spring rolls), cá kho tộ (caramelized fish), and bánh flan for dessert, paired with premium wines

day_by_day.notes: Request a bilingual premium guide for the cultural excursion. Dress modestly when visiting pagodas. Sunscreen and light breathable clothing recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise yoga or meditation session on the beach arranged by the resort. Follow with a premium Vietnamese street food cooking class hosted by a renowned local chef — learn to make bánh mì, fresh spring rolls, and phở broth from scratch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local market with your private guide — taste exotic fruits, sample street snacks, and shop for artisan souvenirs and silk products. Experience the vibrant sights, sounds, and flavors of authentic Vietnamese market culture.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private boat cruise along the coastline at sunset. Enjoy chilled champagne, fresh seafood canapés, and breathtaking ocean views. Return to the resort for a relaxing evening.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-yoga refreshments — herbal tea, fresh fruit, and granola bowls at the resort
meals.lunch: Street food tasting lunch at the local market — bánh xèo (sizzling crepes), bún bò Huế, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Private sunset seafood dinner on the boat — grilled lobster, tiger prawns, and Vietnamese dipping sauces with chilled Sauvignon Blanc

day_by_day.notes: Cooking class ingredients are sourced fresh from the morning market. Boat cruise should be booked in advance through the resort concierge. Bring a light jacket for the evening boat cruise.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided half-day trip to a UNESCO World Heritage site or significant cultural landmark in the region (such as ancient temples, imperial citadels, or historic old towns depending on resort location). Explore with an expert historian guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a traditional Vietnamese village known for a specific craft — lacquerware, silk weaving, or pottery. Participate in a hands-on workshop to create your own souvenir under artisan guidance.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. Enjoy a traditional Vietnamese water puppet show arranged privately or at a nearby cultural center, followed by a premium dinner at a top-rated local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Vietnamese-style breakfast at the resort — bánh cuốn (steamed rice rolls), soft-boiled eggs, and Vietnamese iced coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a heritage restaurant near the cultural site — cao lầu noodles, white rose dumplings, and com hến (clam rice)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a premium local restaurant specializing in regional Vietnamese cuisine — tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the heritage site. Some temples may require removing shoes and covering shoulders/knees. Book water puppet show in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Full-day premium excursion begins — private speedboat or seaplane transfer to a nearby island or bay for a luxury day trip. Explore limestone caves, emerald waters, and hidden lagoons with a private guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling or kayaking in crystal-clear waters around the island. Enjoy a freshly prepared beachside BBQ lunch on a private sandbar. Relax in a premium sun lounger setup arranged by the resort team.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by private transfer. Unwind with a traditional Vietnamese herbal spa treatment — hot stone massage or aromatic body wrap at the resort's luxury spa.

meals.breakfast: Grab-and-go premium breakfast box from the resort — croissants, fresh fruit, yogurt parfait, and cold brew coffee
meals.lunch: Private beachside BBQ on the sandbar — grilled fresh fish, squid, corn, and tropical fruit platter with chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Light spa dinner at the resort's wellness restaurant — lemongrass soup, steamed sea bass, and herbal teas

day_by_day.notes: Confirm weather conditions for the island excursion the evening before. Bring waterproof bags for electronics. Spa booking should be made 24 hours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure — enjoy the resort's private beach, infinity pool, or water sports facilities. Optional: paddleboarding or stand-up kayaking along the coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private cultural tour of a nearby city or town — visit a fine art museum, colonial architecture district, and local temples. End with a curated shopping experience at premium boutiques featuring Vietnamese silk, lacquerware, and handcrafted jewelry.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive rooftop or beachfront dinner at one of the region's most acclaimed fine-dining restaurants. Enjoy a chef's tasting menu celebrating the best of Vietnamese cuisine with international influences.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast buffet — international and Vietnamese stations, freshly made dim sum, smoothie bar, and artisan breads
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at a French-Vietnamese fusion bistro in the city — baguette sandwiches, pâté chaud, and Vietnamese coffee crème brûlée
meals.dinner: Chef's tasting menu at a Michelin-recognized or award-winning restaurant — 7-course Vietnamese progressive cuisine with sommelier-selected wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Reserve the fine-dining restaurant at least 2 days in advance. Dress code at the restaurant is smart casual to formal. Shopping boutiques may accept USD or major credit cards.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided street food walking tour through the most authentic local neighborhoods. Sample iconic Vietnamese street foods — bánh mì, bún chả, bột chiên, and chè (sweet dessert soup) from the best local stalls and hidden gems.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local fishing harbor or riverside area. Board a traditional wooden junk boat for a private river or coastal cruise. Learn about local fishing traditions from seasoned fishermen.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private traditional music performance — Vietnamese đàn tranh (zither) or ca trù (ceremonial singing) arranged by the resort. Followed by dinner at the resort's premium restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Street food breakfast during the morning tour — bánh mì thịt, xôi (sticky rice), and soy milk from local vendors
meals.lunch: Lunch at a riverside restaurant — fresh river fish, morning glory stir-fry, and steamed clams with lemongrass
meals.dinner: Premium dinner at the resort — Vietnamese royal cuisine-inspired dishes such as nem công chả phượng (imperial rolls) and lotus rice, with cocktail pairing

day_by_day.notes: Street food tour guide should be a certified local food expert. Bring small denomination cash for street food purchases. Traditional music performance can be arranged through the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise trek or motorbike tour through scenic countryside, rice paddies, or hill terrain near the resort area. Experience rural Vietnamese life, interact with local farmers, and capture stunning landscape photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a premium coffee plantation or tea estate for a guided tasting experience. Learn about Vietnam's world-famous coffee culture — from Robusta cultivation to the art of brewing egg coffee (cà phê trứng).
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the resort — private bonfire setup on the beach with curated cocktails, live acoustic music, and a premium BBQ dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the resort — energy bars, fresh juice, and Vietnamese-style congee before the morning trek
meals.lunch: Farm-to-table lunch at the coffee or tea estate — fresh local produce, cold brew coffee, and traditional snacks
meals.dinner: Private beachfront BBQ dinner — premium cuts, fresh seafood, artisan cheeses, and craft cocktails under the stars

day_by_day.notes: Motorbike tour requires a valid license or can be done with a private driver. Wear closed-toe shoes for the trek. Bonfire setup should be requested from the resort concierge by noon.

day_by_day.morning: Indulge in a full morning at the resort's luxury spa — choose from a signature Vietnamese herbal ritual, couples' massage, or rejuvenating facial treatment. Followed by a dip in the resort's private plunge pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private photography tour of the most scenic and culturally rich spots in the region — guided by a professional photographer who helps capture stunning portraits, landscapes, and cultural moments. Receive edited digital photos as a keepsake.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gala dinner at the resort — premium private dining experience on the beach with personalized menu, floral setup, candlelight, and live serenade. Celebrate the journey with a curated wine and cocktail selection.

meals.breakfast: Spa morning breakfast — acai bowls, green smoothies, avocado toast, and herbal infusions at the wellness café
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the resort's pool bar — Vietnamese summer rolls, grilled corn, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Exclusive private farewell beach dinner — 5-course Vietnamese and international fusion menu, champagne toast, and a personalized dessert platter

day_by_day.notes: Spa treatments should be booked the day before. Photography tour deliverables (edited photos) may take 24–48 hours. Farewell dinner setup requires advance coordination with the resort events team.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning — enjoy one last breakfast at the resort's beachfront restaurant. Take a peaceful walk along the beach, collect memories, and complete any last-minute souvenir shopping at the resort boutique or nearby market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out from the resort with full concierge assistance for luggage and transfers. Private luxury vehicle transfer to the airport. Enjoy VIP airport lounge access arranged through the resort's premium services.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day premium Vietnam experience filled with culture, cuisine, and coastal luxury.

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast — full Vietnamese and international spread, fresh juices, and a farewell Vietnamese iced coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport VIP lounge or a quick stop at a premium café near the airport
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Request late checkout if flight timing permits (subject to availability). Confirm private airport transfer at least 24 hours before departure. Allow extra time for airport security and check-in procedures.
